name: Block Island National Wildlife Refuge

access.hours: Open daily, sunrise to sunset.
access.pets: Pets are not allowed; service animals are welcome.

activationNotes: Reach Block Island by ferry or plane; the refuge is about four miles from the ferry landing.
Plan for a walk to the North Light and bring drinking water.
Stay out of posted closed areas and designated hunt areas restricted to permitted hunters.

orange.season: During hunting season, generally October through February.
orange.details: The refuge recommends blaze orange for visitors during hunting season. No minimum area is specified.

name: John H. Chafee National Wildlife Refuge

access.hours: Open daily, sunrise to sunset.
access.pets: Pets are not allowed, apart from permitted hunting dogs and service animals.
access.accessibility: The Sprague Bridge kayak launch is not wheelchair or stroller accessible.

activationNotes: Public access is concentrated at the Sprague Bridge kayak launch and designated shoreline access points; there are no managed refuge trails.
The refuge headquarters address is in Charlestown, away from the refuge; use the visitor map to choose an access point.
Hunt units are restricted to permitted hunters.

orange.season: During fall and winter hunting seasons, generally September through January.
orange.details: Wearing orange near active hunting areas is a practical precaution. The refuge does not publish a general orange requirement for ordinary visitors.

name: Ninigret National Wildlife Refuge

access.hours: Trails are open sunrise to sunset. Kettle Pond Visitor Center is open daily, 10 am to 4 pm.
access.parking: Choose the Kettle Pond headquarters or a Salt Pond trail entrance; they are separate parts of the refuge.
access.pets: Leashed dogs are allowed on Kettle Pond Visitor Center trails except Toupoysett Pond Trail. Pets are not allowed on the other refuge trails.

activationNotes: Stay on designated trails and avoid disturbing vegetation.
Salt Pond trails close to general visitors during special deer hunts; check current refuge notices before visiting.
Connecting trails enter Burlingame State Park and Management Area, where different orange rules apply.

orange.season: During hunting seasons: September through January, and April through May in the Barrier Beach and Lewis Tract units.
orange.details: The refuge recommends blaze orange for visitors during hunting season. No minimum area is specified.

name: Sachuest Point National Wildlife Refuge

access.hours: Trails: sunrise to sunset. Visitor center: daily, 10 am to 3 pm. Exterior restroom: 6:30 am to 4:30 pm.
access.parking: Parking at the end of Sachuest Point Road is limited on busy weekends; carpool when possible.
access.pets: Pets are not allowed; trained service animals must remain leashed.
access.accessibility: Flint Point Loop, Island Rocks platform, and the Sakonnet overlook are accessible. Price Neck has steep, rugged terrain.

activationNotes: Bicycles are not allowed on refuge trails; use the racks by the parking area.
Keep equipment clear of trails and protected habitat; check posted refuge rules before setting up.
Occasional special deer hunts may affect access; check refuge notices.

orange.details: No general orange requirement for ordinary refuge visits. Follow posted instructions during any special hunt.

name: Trustom Pond National Wildlife Refuge

access.hours: Trails are open sunrise to sunset, except during posted closures. The contact station opens when volunteers are available.
access.parking: Use the refuge entrance at 1040 Matunuck Schoolhouse Road in South Kingstown.
access.pets: Pets are not allowed; service animals are welcome.
access.accessibility: Restrooms, the contact station, and most trails are wheelchair accessible. Otter Point and Farm Pond platforms are barrier free; Osprey Point has stairs.

activationNotes: The refuge closes to other activities during its limited deer hunting sessions; check the current hunt page before visiting.
Stay on designated trails. There are no picnic areas or campsites, and fires are prohibited.

orange.season: State-managed hunting areas: second Saturday in September through the last day of February, and third Saturday in April through May 31.
orange.details: Field 1 is managed with DEM as part of South Shore Management Area and follows state orange rules. Ordinary refuge trails have no general orange requirement; special deer hunts close the refuge to other visitors.

name: Roger Williams National Memorial

access.hours: Memorial grounds are open dawn to dusk. Visitor center hours vary seasonally.
access.parking: Free visitor parking has a two-hour limit and is for people actively visiting the memorial.
access.pets: Leashed pets are allowed on the grounds; pets are not allowed in public buildings, except service animals.
access.accessibility: Brick paths, a wheelchair-accessible visitor center, accessible restroom stalls, and picnic tables with extended tops.

activationNotes: Stakes, poles, and objects inserted into the ground are prohibited; do not tie or hang equipment from trees.
Generators and inverters require a permit. Park outlets may not be used to charge personal equipment.
Keep radio audio at a reasonable volume and leave pathways clear.

orange.details: Orange clothing is not required for ordinary visits to the memorial grounds.

name: East State Beach

access.hours: Seasonal gates open at 9 a.m. weekdays and 8:30 a.m. weekends/holidays; gates close at sunset.
access.fees: Seasonal beach parking fee; day and season passes are available.
access.pets: Pets are prohibited on state bathing beaches April 1–September 30, except service animals.
access.parking: Small gravel parking lot; spaces can fill early.

activationNotes: Beach facilities and lifeguards are seasonal; plan for reduced amenities after Labor Day.
Use designated dune crossings and keep equipment out of swimming areas.
Sand-trail vehicle access needs a barrier beach permit. Campsites require a self-contained 4WD vehicle; no utility hookups.

orange.season: Second Saturday in September through the last day of February, and third Saturday in April through the last day of May.
orange.details: East Beach/Ninigret Conservation Area is a designated undeveloped state park. Wear at least 200 square inches of solid daylight fluorescent orange above the waist, visible from all directions; 500 square inches during shotgun deer season.

name: Blackstone River Valley National Historical Park
manager: National Park Service and partner site managers

access.hours: Hours vary among Old Slater Mill, state parks, and other partner sites; check the selected destination.
access.parking: Old Slater Mill has visitor parking, including accessible spaces; follow its two-hour parking limit.
access.pets: Leashed pets are allowed on NPS grounds; pets are not allowed in public buildings, except service animals.
access.accessibility: Old Slater Mill has accessible parking, a wheelchair-accessible visitor center and tour entrance, and loaner wheelchairs.

activationNotes: The park includes several separate destinations; choose a specific site before traveling.
On NPS-owned grounds, stakes, poles, and ground-penetrating objects are prohibited; generators and inverters require a permit.
Use the rules of the actual partner property for setup and access.

orange.details: No general orange requirement at the NPS visitor areas. Follow the actual land manager's rules when visiting partner properties.

name: Sapowet Marsh State Wildlife Area

access.hours: 30 minutes before sunrise to 30 minutes after sunset for ordinary visits.

activationNotes: Use designated access points and keep roads, gates, trails, and boat ramps clear.
Organized groups of 10 or more need a DEM special use permit.

orange.season: Second Saturday in September through the last day of February, and third Saturday in April through the last day of May.
